# Polarisation-specific operator audit in response to V1

The first commutator of the encoded polarisation Hamiltonian generally requires local Y and two-qubit YZ/ZY operators. The independent local Y layer used in P remains a plausible variational extension. Its usefulness for final-energy optimisation does not, by itself, demonstrate counterdiabatic suppression of transitions along a polarisation-specific interpolation. A restricted local gauge-potential approximation is also possible, provided its coefficients and residual are explicitly assessed.

This supplements ledger entries 3, 8, 14, 17 and 24 and emmy/product-control-note.md. It does not withdraw the product-state reachability result. The new calculation answers a different question: which generator is motivated by the first commutator, rather than which bitstrings a circuit can represent?

## Source and convention boundary

Inputs/source-metadata.json and inputs/scan-seed.json were re-inspected. Q remains the supplied accepted-manuscript text, DOI 10.1021/acs.jctc.5c01464, with repository cover download date 5 September 2026 and no supplied PDF. Q Eq. 11 motivates the conditional symmetric positive-definite response matrix; its exact extracted Eq. 10 is not certified. P remains the supplied publisher PDF, DOI 10.1103/PhysRevApplied.21.034036, printed publication date 19 March 2024 and correction date 17 June 2024, with metadata manifestation date null. Prior exposure is unchanged: neither source is labelled unseen.

P Sec. II.C, printed p. 034036-5, names a nested-commutator operator pool and selects a local Y term for its Ising formulation. Its independently parameterised circuit is explicit in Fig. 9, printed p. 034036-14. The existing Ghostscript recoveries in emmy/P-page5-recovered.txt and emmy/P-page14-recovered.txt retain their status as derived text from the pinned PDF, not a new visual inspection. Here we define the bit mapping and mixer signs ourselves; no step depends on the defective extracted signs in P Eqs. 1-3.

For external methodological context, [Claeys et al., arXiv:1904.03209v1, Eqs. 1-4](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.03209v1) give a nested-commutator approximation to the adiabatic gauge potential and a variational action. This is established methodology, not a new construction claimed here. Their convention is consistent with adding the schedule velocity times the gauge potential to the driving Hamiltonian. The following polarisation-specific expansion and synthetic checks are derived here. This source was inspected on 29 September 2026. The abstract of [Chandarana et al., arXiv:2107.02789v3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.02789v3), P reference 30, was also inspected for the distinction between CD-inspired ansatz design and exact driving; it is not used to certify any EMLE result.

## From a continuous response to an Ising cost

Fix one geometry and an unscaled variational energy

\[
U(\mu)=\tfrac12\mu^TA\mu-E^T\mu,\qquad A=A^T\succ0,
\qquad \mu=\ell+Bx.
\]

Use the minimisation convention

\[
x_i=(I-Z_i)/2,\qquad d_i=b_i/2,\qquad
m=\ell+\tfrac12\sum_i b_i,\qquad \mu=m-\sum_i d_i Z_i.
\]

Here the columns of the encoding matrix are the vectors \(b_i\). The corresponding diagonal Hamiltonian is

\[
H_C=cI+\sum_i h_iZ_i+\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}Z_iZ_j,
\]
\[
h_i=d_i^T(E-Am),\qquad J_{ij}=d_i^TAd_j,
\qquad c=\tfrac12m^TAm-E^Tm+\tfrac12\sum_i d_i^TAd_i.
\]

Every unordered pair appears once. The identity term affects energies but not commutators or optimised gauge coefficients. A physical energy scale would need to be declared when converting this cost to dimensionless gate angles. Positive definiteness of the continuous response does not remove bit couplings: for two bits in the same component, \(J_{ij}=A_{kk}b_{ki}b_{kj}/4\), which is nonzero even for diagonal \(A\). Molecular dipole couplings create further interactions between components. This derivation concerns the unscaled objective; the energy-normalisation issue in Ada entry 16 remains a separate prerequisite for matching Q.

## First nested commutator

Set \(\hbar=1\), choose fixed positive mixer strengths \(g_i\), and define

\[
H_M=-\sum_i g_iX_i,\qquad
H(\lambda)=(1-\lambda)H_M+\lambda H_C,\qquad
D=\partial_\lambda H=H_C-H_M.
\]

The minus sign makes the product of plus states a ground state of the mixer. The parameter \(\lambda\) here is a circuit interpolation, not an alchemical coordinate or molecular time. With standard Pauli matrices, \([X,Z]=-2iY\). Since

\[
[H,D]=[H_M,H_C],
\]

we obtain the Hermitian direction

\[
K=i[H,D]=-2\left[
\sum_i g_i h_iY_i+
\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}(g_iY_iZ_j+g_jZ_iY_j)
\right].
\]

Thus the first nested-commutator ansatz is \(\mathcal A^{(1)}_\lambda=\alpha(\lambda)K\). Reversing the mixer sign reverses this displayed direction. Independent local and pair angles form an expanded variational pool rather than the single-coefficient first-order ansatz. No XY or YX term is generated at this first order for this diagonal cost and X mixer.

The orthogonal projection of \(K\) onto the local Y span retains only its first sum. Using the normalised Hilbert-Schmidt norm on \(L\) qubits, the squared omitted norm is

\[
\|K-K_{\rm local}\|_{\rm HS}^2
=2^{-L}\operatorname{Tr}[(K-K_{\rm local})^2]
=4\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}^2(g_i^2+g_j^2).
\]

This is an operator omission measure, not a transition-probability or optimisation-error bound. The circuit in P can still produce effective nonlocal generators through composition of its cost and mixer layers. The claim is only that its added local layer is not the full first-commutator generator for a generic coupled polarisation encoding. It is not a no-go result for the whole circuit or its dynamical control algebra.

## A calibrated local alternative is preserved

For a candidate gauge potential define

\[
G=D+i[\mathcal A,H],\qquad S=2^{-L}\operatorname{Tr}(G^2).
\]

An exact gauge potential makes the off-diagonal part of \(G\) vanish in the instantaneous energy basis, equivalently \([H,G]=0\) between distinct eigenspaces. The action retains a diagonal contribution even for an exact solution. At degeneracies it does not specify transport within each degenerate subspace.

For the first direction let \(V=i[K,H]\). Minimising the action over its scalar coefficient gives

\[
\alpha_*=-\frac{\langle D,V\rangle_{\rm HS}}{\langle V,V\rangle_{\rm HS}}
\]

when the denominator is positive. For an independently parameterised local ansatz \(\mathcal A_{\rm local}=\sum_i y_iY_i\), direct Pauli expansion instead gives

\[
y_i^*(\lambda)=\frac{g_i h_i}
{2\left[(1-\lambda)^2g_i^2+\lambda^2\left(h_i^2+\sum_{j\ne i}J_{ij}^2\right)\right]}.
\]

This formula assumes the fixed interpolation above, full trace action, distinct unordered pairs, and a nonzero denominator. It follows because the action has the terms

\[
S=\sum_i(g_i-2\lambda h_i y_i)^2
+\sum_i(h_i-2(1-\lambda)g_i y_i)^2
+\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}^2
+4\lambda^2\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}^2(y_i^2+y_j^2),
\]

up to the omitted constant contribution. All displayed Pauli strings are orthogonal. This provides a legitimate restricted approximation and shows why its coefficients should not be confused with arbitrary final-energy gate angles. A state-weighted action would define another approximation and could change these coefficients.

For a centred grid with zero field, \(m=E=0\), all \(h_i\) vanish. The optimum of this local action is then zero whenever the denominators are positive, whereas the YZ/ZY direction remains nonzero. Equivalently, the global bit-flip parity commutes with \(H\) and \(D\); each local Y is parity odd while YZ/ZY is parity even. A nonzero local Y layer may still be an optimisation heuristic, but this symmetric case gives it no support from the stated gauge action.

## Executed small example

emmy/commutator_check.py uses only the Python standard library and writes emmy/commutator-results.json. The latter records source and script hashes. Run it from the thread root using the available Xcode Python runtime. This is not an imported executable, EMLE reconstruction, QAOA training run, or force calculation.

The synthetic scalar response is \(A=1\), with encoding \(\mu=-1.5+x_0+2x_1\). Thus \(m=0\), \(d=(0.5,1)\), \(c=0.625\) and \(J=0.5\). Fields \(E=0\) and \(E=0.4\) give respectively \(h=(0,0)\) and \(h=(0.2,0.4)\). All quantities are dimensionless. The grid excludes zero; it is deliberately an operator example and carries no hydration-bias interpretation.

Dense four-dimensional matrices independently verify all four encoded energies, the commutator signs and coefficients, independence of the first commutator from interpolation position, the local projection norm, and stationarity of both gauge-action fits at \(\lambda\in\{0,0.37,1\}\). The largest recorded numerical discrepancy is below \(2.3\times10^{-15}\).

At zero field the exact direction is \(K=-(Y_0Z_1+Z_0Y_1)\), with zero local projection and squared omitted norm 2. At \(\lambda=0.37\), the no-gauge and best local-gauge actions both equal 2.25. The fitted first-commutator coefficient is approximately -0.154147334, reducing the action to 1.941705332; the squared gauge-equation residual is approximately \(6.2\times10^{-33}\). In this small case the two-body direction satisfies the exact off-diagonal gauge equation, subject to the degeneracy qualification above. No annealing evolution or fidelity was simulated.

With field 0.4 at the same interpolation point, the local fit is nonzero and reduces the action from 2.45 to approximately 2.005204896. The first-direction fit reaches approximately 1.925984128 but its squared gauge-equation residual is approximately 0.517741424. Thus the nonzero-field first-order ansatz is not exact even in this small example. An action reduction must not be reported as measured suppression of transitions, a molecular energy improvement, or quantum advantage.

## What is and is not justified

V1 now has an explicit cost mapping, mixer convention, derived first commutator, restricted local alternative, and an executable check. The practical comparison should retain the transferred independent local Y ansatz as a CD-inspired variational extension, alongside a polarisation-specific Y/YZ/ZY construction with either calibrated gauge coefficients or separately declared variational coefficients. The latter generally adds entangling operations; the no-extra-two-qubit-gates property of the local layer in P cannot be assumed for this construction.

Calling a transferred run an approximation to counterdiabatic driving still requires a specified interpolation and schedule, calibrated coefficients or another explicit approximation rationale, and an assessment of the omitted terms. A digitised driving claim also requires relating gates to the added term \(\dot\lambda\mathcal A_\lambda\), with Trotter and finite-step errors controlled. A causal claim that transition suppression explains an optimisation gain needs dynamical or spectral evidence beyond final QUBO scores. None of those gains was measured here.

The previously established energy, readout, force and classical-product controls remain necessary. Real response matrices, publication-specific scaling, physically useful precision and total comparator costs remain unresolved in this calculation. Ada is independently handling the bounded publication-input audit requested in V2. No scientific verdict or publication novelty is awarded by this note.

import hashlib, itertools, json, math
from fractions import Fraction as F
from pathlib import Path
# Self-defined dimensionless scalar response, not an EMLE configuration.
def u(mu): return mu*mu/2+F(51,100)*mu
bits=list(itertools.product((0,1),repeat=2))
mus=[F(-2+x+2*y) for x,y in bits]
costs=[u(m) for m in mus]
rows=[]
for t in [F(k,100) for k in range(101)]:
    probs=[(t if x else 1-t)*(1-t if y else t) for x,y in bits]
    mean=sum(p*m for p,m in zip(probs,mus))
    mean_u=u(mean); expected=sum(p*v for p,v in zip(probs,costs))
    variance=sum(p*(m-mean)**2 for p,m in zip(probs,mus))
    assert mean == -t and variance == 5*t*(1-t)
    assert expected == mean_u+variance/2 == F(199,100)*t-2*t*t
    correlated=(1-t)*u(F(0))+t*u(F(-1))
    assert correlated == -t/100
    assert correlated == mean_u+t*(1-t)/2
    rows.append(dict(t=str(t),product_expectation=str(expected),mean_energy=str(mean_u),correlated_expectation=str(correlated)))
t_peak=F(199,400); barrier=F(39601,80000)
assert F(199,100)*t_peak-2*t_peak*t_peak==barrier
# Exact distribution of sample-mean energy for up to three independent shots.
t=F(51,100)
probs=[(t if x else 1-t)*(1-t if y else t) for x,y in bits]
shot_rows=[]
for count in (1,2,3):
    observed=F(0)
    for seq in itertools.product(range(4),repeat=count):
        prob=math.prod(probs[k] for k in seq)
        observed+=prob*u(sum(mus[k] for k in seq)/count)
    theory=u(-t)+5*t*(1-t)/(2*count)
    assert observed==theory
    shot_rows.append(dict(shots=count,enumerated_outcome_sequences=4**count,expected_mean_energy=str(observed),predicted=str(theory)))
# Local-angle Hessian at each strict bit minimum, independently finite differenced.
hessians=[]
for state in range(4):
    gaps=[costs[state^(1<<j)]-costs[state] for j in range(2)]
    if all(v>0 for v in gaps):
        eps=1e-4
        numerical=[2*float(g)*math.sin(eps/2)**2/eps**2 for g in gaps]
        assert max(abs(v-float(g)/2) for v,g in zip(numerical,gaps))<1e-8
        hessians.append(dict(bits=bits[state],mu=str(mus[state]),cost=str(costs[state]),flip_gaps=list(map(str,gaps)),hessian_diagonal=[str(g/2) for g in gaps],finite_difference=numerical))
# Homotopy from uncoupled coordinates to the inherited axis-aligned two-site model.
continuation=[]
for eta in (F(0),F(1,4),F(1,2),F(1)):
    a=[[F(int(i==j)) for j in range(6)] for i in range(6)]
    for j,tensor in enumerate((F(2,125),F(-1,125),F(-1,125))):
        a[j][j+3]=a[j+3][j]=-eta*tensor
    target=[F(-51,100)]*6
    field=[sum(v*m for v,m in zip(row,target)) for row in a]
    def energy(mu): return sum(mu[i]*sum(a[i][j]*mu[j] for j in range(6))/2-field[i]*mu[i] for i in range(6))
    # Integer comparison with common denominator avoids tolerance-dependent traps.
    vals=[]
    for index in range(4096):
        mu=[F(((index>>(2*i))&3)-2) for i in range(6)]
        vals.append(energy(mu))
    minima=[i for i,v in enumerate(vals) if all(v<vals[i^(1<<j)] for j in range(12))]
    near=[i for i,v in enumerate(vals) if all(v<vals[i+step*(1<<(2*j))] for j in range(6) for step in (-1,1) if 0<=((i>>(2*j))&3)+step<4)]
    assert len(minima)==64 and len(near)==1
    mincurv=min((vals[i^(1<<j)]-vals[i])/2 for i in minima for j in range(12))
    assert mincurv>0
    # For g_i=1, squared omitted first-commutator norm is 8*sum J_ij**2.
    inside=outside=F(0)
    for i in range(12):
        for j in range(i+1,12):
            jij=a[i//2][j//2]*2**(i%2)*2**(j%2)/4
            if i//2==j//2: inside+=8*jij*jij
            else: outside+=8*jij*jij
    assert inside==12
    continuation.append(dict(eta=str(eta),strict_bit_minima=len(minima),adjacent_level_minima=len(near),minimum_product_angle_curvature=str(mincurv),first_commutator_intra_component_pair_norm_squared=str(inside),first_commutator_inter_component_pair_norm_squared=str(outside),states_enumerated=len(vals)))
result=dict(scope="New synthetic dimensionless cross-branch calculation; no molecular input, trained P circuit, annealing, force, free energy or resource advantage",scalar=dict(A=1,E="-51/100",encoding="mu=-2+x0+2*x1",continuous_energy=str(u(F(-51,100))),grid_minimum=str(min(costs))),scalar_path=rows,product_path_maximum=dict(t=str(t_peak),barrier_from_suboptimal_zero=str(barrier)),basis_hessians=hessians,sample_mean_checks=shot_rows,coupling_continuation=continuation,script_sha256=hashlib.sha256(Path(__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest())
Path("emmy/carry-results.json").write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+"\n")
print(json.dumps({k:v for k,v in result.items() if k!="scalar_path"},indent=2))

# Observable certification and encoding controls for Q010-P011

The supported decision is to pause production replacement of the EMLE solve. A defensible research question is whether an apparent DCQAOA improvement survives a verified physical-energy contract and classical controls that preserve the structure of the dipole problem. The joint investigation adds a concrete connection: the binary traps of branch 3 are strict product-state training minima, and correlations can remove a carry-path barrier even with no physical coupling. A classical correlated update removes the same barrier. Separately, Ada derives a mixed-field observable correction that is certifiable but is a saddle if jointly optimised. These are conditional synthetic results and a sharper experiment, not molecular improvement, quantum advantage or established publication novelty.

Source evidence and inherited boundaries

Q is the retained repository peer-reviewed/accepted manuscript, DOI 10.1021/acs.jctc.5c01464, with cover-sheet download date 5 September 2026. Its raw and retained text are identical. No Q PDF is supplied. Manuscript pp. 13-14, Eqs. 9-13, motivate induced dipoles, a half-interaction energy and dielectric scaling; the redundant summation in extracted Eq. 10 remains uncertified. We define conditional algebra independently rather than repairing missing primary evidence. Q pp. 24-29 reports patched hydration RMSE 1.63 kcal/mol, OpenFF/TIP3P RMSE 0.80, and empirically scaled RMSE 0.74. The last comparison is reported as statistically indistinguishable at the stated confidence level, not a demonstrated superiority. Q pp. 17-18 identifies reference-data generation as a training bottleneck, not the induced-dipole solve.

P is the author-supplied publisher PDF, DOI 10.1103/PhysRevApplied.21.034036, printed publication date 19 March 2024 and correction date 17 June 2024; metadata manifestation date remains null. Sec. II.C, printed p. 034036-5, explicitly specifies the full-parameter circuits and added local Y layer. Fig. 9 and its caption, p. 034036-14, specify independent RZ/RX/RY rotations. Sec. III reports simulations on selected pharmacophore graphs, not hydration or hardware advantage. The supplied correction concerns interchanged figures. P is a known campaign-1 calibration source; Q has prior scanning and retained-input exposure. Neither is unseen.

All branch copies of source inputs are byte-identical. New Ghostscript extraction of PDF pages 5 and 14 and the complete PDF matches the inherited extractions exactly. This verifies derivation from the pinned bytes, not visual glyph fidelity. The 21 uncorrected page records join exactly to P.txt. The abstract-correction provenance file named by metadata is absent locally; no reconstruction of it is claimed. The retained PNG was not visually inspected. No inference depends on defective docking inequalities, penalty signs or the questionable Q summation. The original scan was an abstract-based hypothesis for P and its numerical scores are not evidence.

The inherited research is complementary rather than independent replication of the source papers:

- branches/branch-1/ledger.jsonl entries 5, 8, 13 and 24-29, branches/branch-1/emmy/product-control-note.md and branches/branch-1/emmy/commutator-note.md give the covariance identity, product-state control and first-commutator audit.
- branches/branch-2/ledger.jsonl entries 25-31 and branches/branch-2/ada/v1-implementation-audit.md distinguish solve and readout fields and record the publication-input blocker. The later engine revision is not the Q implementation.
- branches/branch-3/ledger.jsonl entries 20-27, branches/branch-3/emmy/encoding-audit.md and branches/branch-3/ada/two-site-audit.md give corrected residual costs, explicit two-site dipole structure, binary traps and a rounding failure.

The axis-aligned count of 729 finer-grid minima and the rotated count of 64 are compatible: their geometry and grid ranges differ. The axis-aligned fine results use proved pair factorisation; the rotated grids trim their domains. Neither demonstrates general asymptotic scaling. Rounding succeeds on their refinement fields but fails on a separate nearby field by 0.006968, so it is a comparator, not an exact general algorithm. Full variational grid energies are continuous envelopes with possible force jumps; discontinuous forces alone do not imply a nonconservative potential. Reusing the stationary half-interaction formula can instead introduce energy jumps and an incorrect limiting within-cell derivative.

New connection: product-state traps and correlations

For a diagonal encoded cost with value \(f(x)\), let \(x\) be a strict single-bit minimum. Parameterise nearby product states by local rotations \(R_Y(\delta_j)\) acting on that basis state. Since flip probabilities are \(\sin^2(\delta_j/2)\),

\[
C(\delta)=f(x)+\frac14\sum_j\left[f(x\oplus e_j)-f(x)\right]\delta_j^2+O(\|\delta\|^4).
\]

Its angle Hessian is diagonal with entries \([f(x\oplus e_j)-f(x)]/2>0\). Thus branch-3 bit traps are strict local minima of the branch-1 product-angle objective. This is a local product-family statement, not a Hessian theorem for the complete entangling P circuit. Both full P ansatze contain every basis optimum, but that representability does not guarantee discovery.

An exact scalar example makes the competing paths explicit:

\[
U(\mu)=\mu^2/2+0.51\mu,\qquad \mu=-2+x_0+2x_1.
\]

The continuous optimum is \(-0.51\), with energy \(-0.13005\). Grid values zero and minus one correspond to bitstrings differing in both bits; zero is suboptimal but a strict bit and product-angle minimum. The best grid energy is \(-0.01\).

Along independent probabilities \(p_0=t,p_1=1-t\), the mean is \(-t\), but the decoded variance is \(5t(1-t)\). Hence

\[
C_{\rm product}(t)=U(-t)+\frac52t(1-t)=1.99t-2t^2.
\]

This particular path from zero to minus one reaches an energy barrier of \(39601/80000=0.4950125\) at \(t=199/400\). It is not a minimax barrier claim over every product path. A correlated distribution supported only on the endpoint strings, with probabilities \(1-t,t\), has the same mean, variance \(t(1-t)\), and

\[
C_{\rm correlated}(t)=(1-t)U(0)+tU(-1)=-0.01t.
\]

It descends monotonically. A coherent two-string superposition has the same diagonal expectation, but the classical mixture already supplies this path. No assertion is made that the particular P circuit or first-commutator generator discovers or implements it at favourable cost. The experiment should retain classical updates between adjacent dipole levels or a correlated distribution within each component; a product-only comparator can otherwise overstate the significance of correlations between encoding bits.

A concrete classical comparator groups all bits of each dipole component. For independent component distributions with means \(m_i\) and second moments \(q_i\), its exact expectation is \(U(m)+\tfrac12\sum_i A_{ii}(q_i-m_i^2)\). This permits correlations between bits within a component without quantum sampling. Holding the other components fixed, the conditional energy for a level \(v\) is \(A_{ii}v^2/2+v(\sum_{j\ne i}A_{ij}m_j-E_i)\); on a uniform bounded grid its best level is the clipped nearest level to \((E_i-\sum_{j\ne i}A_{ij}m_j)/A_{ii}\). Thus a component update crosses carries directly. Dense residual maintenance costs linear work per updated component and quadratic work per sweep after matrix construction. General correlated distributions across components need extra representation and cannot be declared cheap by this formula. No universal convergence or global discrete optimality is claimed.

New executable evidence is emmy/carry_control.py and emmy/carry-results.json. Rational enumeration verifies every point of a 101-point path, local Hessians with an independent finite difference, and all outcome sequences for one, two and three independent shots. For the six-component axis-aligned two-site construction, we additionally set \(A_\eta=[I,-\eta T;-\eta T,I]\), \(T=\operatorname{diag}(2,-1,-1)/125\), and \(E_\eta=A_\eta(-0.51\mathbf1)\). The continuous solution and encoding stay fixed; the artificial field changes with coupling. This is not a fixed-field molecular experiment.

Full enumeration of 4096 states at each \(\eta\in\{0,1/4,1/2,1\}\) gives 64 strict bit/product minima and one strict adjacent-level minimum. Their smallest product-angle curvature remains positive, from 0.49 to 0.48216. Using the branch-1 convention \(K=i[H,\partial_\lambda H]\), unit X-mixer strengths and normalised Hilbert-Schmidt norm, the pair contribution from bits within individual components has squared norm 12 even at zero physical coupling. The intercomponent contribution is \(3\eta^2/625\), at most 0.0048 here. Thus pair operators can be dominated by encoding the self-energy. These norm values are not bounds on transition probabilities, trainability or molecular error.

Readout and the physical contract

For SPD \(A\), any fixed distribution of encoded dipoles satisfies

\[
\mathbb E U(\mu)=U(\bar\mu)+\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(A\Sigma),\qquad
\mathbb E U(\widehat\mu_M)=U(\bar\mu)+\frac{\operatorname{tr}(A\Sigma)}{2M}.
\]

The second equality assumes independent shots from a fixed trained distribution. In the scalar example, \(t=0.51\) makes the mean exactly optimal; product finite-shot mean-energy bias is \(0.62475/M\). The correlated distribution gives \(0.12495/M\). Neither changes the best bitstring energy. Optimising the energy of the mean is a distinct convex-box problem in probability coordinates, classically evaluable; it is not minimisation of the usual QUBO expectation. Training randomness, adaptive stopping, correlated hardware noise and force estimators require separate analysis. Born samples are not a canonical solvent ensemble.

Ada joint ledger entries 5 and 8, ada/mixed-field-note.md and ada/mixed_field.py extend the observable audit when the response solves \(A\mu_*=E_s\) but reports \(H_*=-E_0^T\mu_*/2\). With an approximate adjoint \(z\), define

\[
L(\mu,z)=\tfrac12(z^TA\mu-E_0^T\mu-E_s^Tz),\quad
r_s=A\mu-E_s,\quad r_0=Az-E_0.
\]

Then \(L-H_*=r_0^TA^{-1}r_s/2\), bounded in magnitude by \(\|r_0\|\|r_s\|/(2a)\) for certified \(0<a\leq\lambda_{\min}(A)\). It is exact if either vector is exact. Same-field restriction \(z=\mu\) recovers the variational energy; uniform scaling with \(z=\mu/c\) recovers the compatible branch-2 functional. Independent primal and adjoint variables instead give Hessian eigenvalues \(\pm\lambda_i(A)/2\). Joint minimisation is invalid. I independently re-derived this and replayed every partner assertion and output field; emmy/ada-mixed-field-check.json records the check. Coarse correction can worsen actual error and does not guarantee smooth forces.

A coherent next experiment

Acquire a publication-matched text fixture containing ordered response matrix, solve and readout fields, reference dipoles and induction energy with units, dielectric convention and implementation revision. Model bytes, solute and MM coordinates, charges, cutoff/image rules and patches are additionally required for independent physical reconstruction; derivatives are required for force tests. The inherited [supporting-data launcher](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/michellab/EMLE_HFE_SI/0279424ec1770e155533af6247f28ebca98b72b5/inputs/ml_mm_elec/run_fes.sh) and [later engine implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chemle/emle-engine/787617c67391592466491efe276cc2ce267f0019/emle/models/_emle_base.py) are recorded access evidence in branches/branch-2/ada/v1-implementation-audit.md, not newly downloaded or publication-compatible inputs in this call. The model transport failures do not show that files are absent remotely.
